What are some good books to get more into Russian literature?
Can't say I have read much Russian literature but The Brothers Karamazov is an old favorite of mine.

Roadside picnic, a good fiction short story, as for classics, my favorites are The Idiot by Dostoyevsky, The Master and Margarita by Bulgakov although his writing style is not for everyone but to me it was entertaining, then there's Lolita by Nabokov which became known mostly due to the subject it entertains. One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich by Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn

Obviously there should be prerequisites to this, like that the user would have to be at least 30 days old, in good standing, a certain amount of points, etc. But for people like me who are fluent in CSS, it would be fun to be able to style our profiles.

Just a thought.
Allow users to style their profiles the same way subverse admins can style their subverses

I actually really like this idea, it would kind of merge the ideas of Reddit and MySpace or Bebo together so that you could have your personalised user page and could connect more personally with other users and then you'd leave the subverses as they are. Unfortunately I can't CSS for shit but it'd be cool to see the work of others and I'm sure I could pick up enough to get by!

You could write a very simple chrome plugin to replace any CSS you like on the entire domain automatically.

This contains most of the information you need to know: https://developer.chrome.com/extensions/getstarted

I was tempted to do it, but as far as colours and styles go, I'm not sure what people would want.
That's only visible locally though. I'm talking styling our profiles like we can style subverses so that people who visit our profiles see the styles.
oh ok, i can see that being very abused if not done right, and could be a large drain on resources

Anything can be abused, but I don't think that's sufficient reason not to do it. There's already a working model in place.

I don't see how it would be a drain on resources. It's already done with the subverses, and besides, creating a simple custom CSS for each user and then giving them a field to edit and append that file requires virtually zero computational power. It's pretty much the same as allowing you to edit fields in your profile.

As for rendering the CSS, the profile page already does that; it requires zero extra power to import the custom css file.

Subverses only require a single cache file per verse, this would require an additional cache file per user which could get kind of large if this site ever takes off like reddit, each cache could also then potentially be transmitted to every single user on the website (probably not but i'm going to extremes here, because thats what you need to do when calculating costs).

I think you're misunderstanding me, it requires extra server storage and bandwidth space, nobody cares massively about the load on the browser (as it's mostly going to be tiny compared to the rest of the site). Then there's the additional computation power to sanitize it, it would increase costs for the servers quite a bit if this became quite a widely used website.

I'm not saying it's a bad idea, i'm just saying there's considerations that may make it less than desirable to do right now.

You're right, there definitely will ultimately be a lot more users than subverses, and with each one requiring its own stylesheet, even kilobytes will add up over time.

I don't know how drastically it would increase costs, but certainly at least some. I do think it should be restricted only to users who meet certain criteria though, so that could help.
It would certainly need fairly large restrictions in it in any case.
